title: GTA 6 Take-Two stock jumps after rave reviews
description: GTA 6 Take-Two stock rose nearly 7% pre-market after rave reviews, yet shares are still down close to 20% in 2026, according to GameSpot's report.

body.text: The GTA 6 Take-Two stock story is a reminder that big game launches move real money. According to GameSpot, Take-Two shares rose nearly 7% in pre-market trading after reviews for GTA 6 went live, and kept climbing as the day went on, adding billions to the company's market cap. The catch is that the stock is still well below where it started the year.
Why the GTA 6 Take-Two stock jumped

GameSpot says GTA 6 is now available in at least New Zealand and Australia, more than 10 years after fans first started waiting. Reviews have been overwhelmingly positive, and investors clearly noticed.

GameSpot's own review gave the game a rare 10/10. On Metacritic, GTA 6 has taken over from the Ocarina of Time remake for Switch 2 as the highest-rated game of 2026. It is also tied with the original Ocarina of Time for the highest aggregate review score ever, per GameSpot.
Analysts had expected the share price to rise heading into launch, according to the report.
Today's pop does not erase a rough 2026. GameSpot reports Take-Two is down close to 20% this year and roughly 15% over the past 12 months.

The publication points to an earlier hit this year, when Google announced new AI software for making games. That presumably spooked investors, and the stock has not recovered since. GameSpot is blunt that nobody really knows the exact reason, noting that the stock market is fickle.
The long game for Take-Two investors
Zoom out and the picture looks very different. GameSpot cites Rand Group, which points out that $10,000 invested in Take-Two when GTA 5 launched in 2013 has grown to more than $120,000 today.

Many analysts expect the stock to climb further, according to the report, thanks to the expected arrival of GTA Online and a PC edition of GTA 6 in 2027. Those are expectations rather than confirmed dates, so treat the timing with caution.

Keep an eye on whether Take-Two's share price holds its gains once launch-day excitement settles, and whether it can close the gap on its year-to-date losses. For players, the bigger questions are when GTA Online arrives and when the PC version follows. GameSpot says both are expected in 2027, but nothing beyond that has been confirmed in its report.

faqs.q: Why did the GTA 6 Take-Two stock go up?
faqs.a: According to GameSpot, Take-Two shares rose nearly 7% in pre-market trading after overwhelmingly positive GTA 6 reviews landed, and they moved higher as the day went on.

faqs.q: Is Take-Two stock still down in 2026?
faqs.a: Yes. GameSpot reports Take-Two is down close to 20% so far in 2026 and about 15% over the past 12 months, despite the jump after the GTA 6 reviews.

faqs.q: What is the GTA 6 Metacritic score situation?
faqs.a: GameSpot says GTA 6 has overtaken the Ocarina of Time remake for Switch 2 as the highest-rated game of 2026 on Metacritic. It is also tied with the original Ocarina of Time for the highest aggregate review score ever.
